claims: IPAWS is FEMA's national, internet-based infrastructure.
IPAWS allows federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial authorities to send urgent, life-saving alerts to the public.
IPAWS simultaneously delivers alerts via wireless emergency alerts (cell phones), the Emergency Alert System (radio/TV), and NOAA weather radio.
IPAWS enables alerting authorities to send a single message that is distributed instantly to multiple communication channels.
IPAWS delivers geo-targeted warnings to specific geographic areas.
IPAWS provides a secure, internet-based interface for local authorities to send warnings directly to mobile devices and local broadcast channels.
IPAWS supports warnings such as Amber Alerts.
IPAWS supports warnings such as imminent threat alerts.
IPAWS supports various alert types, including weather emergencies, public health, and missing persons.
Authorized public safety officials called Collaborative Operating Groups or COGs utilize IPAWS to issue warnings.
Messages issued through IPAWS are pushed to cell phone carriers.
Messages issued through IPAWS are pushed to media outlets.
